subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: What policy should OpenClaw use for automatic remote skill bin probing on macOS app-backed nodes that may be co-located, still becoming ready, or intermittently remote?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the fix can change default remote-skill eligibility, node exec exposure, startup timing, and operator expectations.

options.title: Defer and back off probes
options.body: Keep app-node `system.which` support, but delay initial probing until node readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff after failures.

options.title: Skip co-located app nodes
options.body: Avoid probing loopback or same-host app nodes while continuing to probe remote macOS nodes that can provide skill binaries.

options.title: Disable app-node probing by default
options.body: Remove automatic app-node remote skill eligibility unless explicitly enabled, reducing warnings at the cost of default remote macOS skill support.

recommendation.title: Defer and back off probes
recommendation.body: Keep app-node `system.which` support, but delay initial probing until node readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff after failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans the remote skills runtime, gateway node command policy, and macOS app-node execution behavior around this decision.
